subject: Dedicated GPU rightsizing + streaming checklist — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@aventihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU rightsizing + streaming checklist — follow-up & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo and the call earlier. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we stay tight on SLOs and sizing for the dedicated pilot.

Summary of requirements from our call:
- Target 99th pct latency: <= 150 ms for a 512-token streaming completion (low-latency path)
- Expected steady-state throughput: 180 requests/min (3 rps) with spikes to 2000 requests/min during peak campaign windows (~33 rps)
- Concurrency: ~40 simultaneous active streaming sessions (long-lived connections with chunked responses)
- Average generation length: 220 tokens output, typically streaming in 50–100 token chunks
- Model family preference: 63B–70B open weights (customer wants to avoid closed models)

Immediate asks / proposed pilot plan:
1) Redwood to run a short dedicated pilot with reserved throughput sizing (we propose: baseline RU for 30 rps with 2x burst headroom).
2) Engineering validation: run latency/throughput bench across 3 hardware configs (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and 8-bit-quant on L4-style cards) for your typical prompts. Karthik, Ben — can we get this bench scoped?
3) Production constraints: encryption/KMS and audit logging are priority; procurement will need an early estimate for committed monthly capacity.
4) Next meeting: schedule a 30-min sizing sync after bench results.

Attachments: discovery notes (ma-discovery-notes.pdf) with sample prompts and expected payloads. I also shared a HubSpot link to the deal above.

Proposed next steps for Aventi: please confirm the expected 99th pct latency target above and whether the peak behavior (33 rps bursts) is an accurate representation of weekends/marketing surges.

Thanks — I can also schedule the bench kickoff if you confirm spike windows.

—
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU rightsizing + streaming checklist — follow-up & next steps

Thanks Lauren — that recap aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 99th pct latency: correct, our user-facing SLA target is 150 ms. For background tasks (non-interactive), we can accept higher latency, but interactive chat must meet that target.
- Burst profile: the 33 rps bursts are concentrated in 10–15 minute windows, 2–3x/day during campaign peaks; typical daytime activity is closer to 4–6 rps.
- Model choice: we're open to 63B family or smaller if the quality/latency tradeoff is acceptable. Cost is a consideration — we'd prefer the most cost-effective config that meets the SLA.

Two asks on our side: 
1) Please include an estimate for committed RU/month and an example billing profile for a 6-month reserved contract.
2) We'd like a short list of mitigation plans if the 99th pct drifts above target (fallback models, autoscale thresholds, and routing policies).

Happy to have Derek and procurement loop in on the pilot commercial terms.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product | Aventi Health

Bench scope request (please confirm ETA and test plan):
- Three hardware configs to evaluate: H100-80GB (best-effort low latency), A100-80GB (cost/perf baseline), and an 8-bit quantized L4-equivalent (cost-optimized).
- Workloads: steady-state at 4 rps, sustained at 30 rps, and spike bursts to 33 rps for 15 minutes.
- Targets to measure: 50/95/99 pctl latency for the first token and full completion, tokens/sec throughput, GPU util, memory/kv cache behavior during streaming, and p99 tail during sustained bursts.
- Deliverables: latency-bench-3configs.csv (raw results) + short summary with recommended reserved RU and suggested autoscale buffer.

Ben — could you own the initial bench run + CSV? Karthik — can you produce the final recommendation with sizing (reserved RU, concurrency buckets, and preferred GPU type) and a short fallback plan (model variant for graceful degradation)?

Proposed timeline: bench started by Fri (2026-10-23), results by Mon EOD (2026-10-26). Let me know if that's realistic.

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 5:05 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Ben — forwarding Aventi's confirmations. Key asks for the bench scope below; I've attached the discovery notes with sample prompt sets.

Quick tech readout and recommendation based on similar pilots we ran: 

1) Bench approach (confirmed)
- Ben will run 3 configs with identical prompt sets and the same batch/streaming harness; we'll collect first-token latency and completion latency distributions.

2) Early recommendation (subject to actual bench numbers)
- If the 99th pct completion latency for 512 tokens is <= 150 ms on H100 with a per-request batch size of 1 and continuous KV cache enabled, choose H100-80GB for the pilot (favored for headroom on long contexts and aggressive concurrency).
- If A100 achieves p99 <= 150 ms consistently but with higher GPU util, A100 is the cost-effective choice (recommendation: pick A100 and increase reserved RU by 20% for safety).
- L4/8-bit quant path is viable only if model quality tests pass; it should be treated as fallback/cost-optimized option, not primary for interactive SLA.

3) Sizing heuristics for Aventi (initial reserved commit)
- Baseline reserved RU: sized for 30 rps sustained with a 2x buffer for burst handling (i.e., reserve for 60 rps equivalence). This maps to roughly 1 x H100 or 1–2 x A100 depending on model size and micro-batching.
- Concurrency plan: allocate 50 concurrent streaming slots with per-slot KV cache pinned; autoscale policy to add additional nodes at 70% GPU util sustained for 2 minutes.

4) Fallback & mitigation
- Canary routing to a smaller 30B model variant if p99 > 200 ms for 3 consecutive minutes; this keeps service available while reducing resource pressure.
- Use prefix caching for common seed prompts to cut repeated token generation during campaign bursts.

5) Deliverables & ETA
- Ben: run bench today–Mon with CSV + short narrative (latency-bench-3configs.csv).
- I'll draft a short recommendation doc mapping bench numbers to committed RU and a sample 6-month billing profile for procurement.

I'll attach the recommendation doc once Ben uploads results. If Aventi confirms the burst windows, we'll time the bench to hit those spike patterns.

—
